US electricity prices are skyrocketing.

The average price of US residential electricity has risen +11% since January 2025, to 19.6 cents per kilowatt-hour in August 2026, near an all-time high.

Average prices during the first 8 months of 2026 were +40% higher than in the same period of 2019.

The largest increase in residential electricity prices over this period was in Maine, at +90%, followed by California and New York, at nearly +70%.

This comes as the AI boom is intensifying electricity demand, with data centers requiring enormous amounts of electricity to power thousands of chips and cooling systems. 

A 1-gigawatt data center can consume as much electricity as 800,000 homes.

As a result, wholesale electricity prices in areas near significant data center activity surged by as much as +267% between 2020 and 2025.

The AI revolution is driving a surge in electricity demand, and households are increasingly feeling the cost.

Corporate earnings growth is set to slow:

10 of the 11 sectors in the S&P 500 are estimated to record lower YoY earnings growth in Q3 2026, compared to Q2.

The Consumer Discretionary sector is expected to post the largest slowdown, from +91% YoY in Q2 to just +2% YoY in Q3.

This is followed by Communication Services, with projected Q3 earnings growth at +66%, down from +126%.

Earnings growth in the Financials sector is estimated to decrease to +2.4% from +22.3%.

Energy and Information Technology, the two best-performing S&P 500 sectors, are expected to see earnings growth decline from +147.8% to +122.5% and from +77.9% to +65.9%, respectively.

We are set for an eventful earnings season.

BREAKING: China’s trade surplus jumped +$67 billion YoY in the first 9 months of 2026, or +7.7%, to a record $938 billion.

This marks its 3rd consecutive YoY increase for this period of the year, totalling +$318 billion.

In September alone, China's trade surplus rose +$50 billion YoY, or +51%, to $134 billion, its 2nd-largest on record.

Exports soared +36% YoY and imports jumped +31%.

At the same time, high-tech shipments surged +64% YoY, accounting for ~50% of total export growth, as global AI infrastructure demand boosted hardware exports.

China’s trade surplus is now on track to exceed the $1.2 trillion record set in 2025.

China is expanding global trade at an unprecedented pace.

BREAKING: Average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving are up +31% YoY, to $402, the highest in at least 10 years.

This marks the 3rd consecutive annual increase, totaling +$133, or +49%.

Since the 2020 pandemic, average domestic round-trip fares for Thanksgiving travel have more than doubled.

By comparison, average round-trip airfares for Christmas are up +23% YoY.

This comes as jet fuel prices have risen +91% since the Iran War began, to ~$4.50 per gallon, driving up airlines’ operating costs.

Americans are facing their priciest holiday travel season in years.

A couple other interesting points: 

a) the temporary concerns about the sector and higher financing costs greatly reduce the risk of overbuild and a collapse in pricing.

b) robotics plus the agent economy will drive a 24x increase in demand/usage in the next few years

BREAKING: US margin debt jumped +$26 billion in September, to $1.48 trillion, the 2nd-highest level on record.

Since the start of 2026, margin debt has surged +$255 billion, or +21%.

As a % of GDP, this metric is up to a record 4.5%, surpassing the previous peak of 3.6% set in 2021.

At the same time, the margin debt-to-M2 money supply ratio is up to 6.3%, the 3rd-highest level on record.

By comparison, this ratio peaked at 6.4% during the 2000 Dot-Com Bubble.

Leveraged investing has never been more popular.
